name: Attainable Sink Set
definition: For a corner-peelable ample family $A$, $\operatorname{Sink}(A)$ is the set of vertices $a\in A$ for which some complete corner peeling of $A$ ends at $a$. Equivalently, these are the possible global sinks of acyclic unique-sink orientations corresponding to corner peelings.
codomain: Vertex subsets, considered with their induced one-inclusion graphs
normalization: Attainability is existential over complete corner peelings; no particular peeling order is part of the value.
comments: The attainable sink set need not be ample, isometric, or connected. It is distinct from the set of geometric corners and from the sink set of one fixed orientation.
